These controls could be developed either by a Tribal land-use commission or by an existing or future area-wide land use commission.
The impact of deferring the development of coal until viable land-\nuse controls are effective would include reduction in income to the
Indians in the short term. In the longer term, such actions would
protect the contemporary culture of the Indian from undue change and
would also lessen the impact on the land through land-use controls.

Deferrment of expanded coal production while land-use controls are being
developed, must be done very soon if the Crow tribe wishes Westmoreland
to remain in continued operation. The coal reserves on Westmoreland's
current mining operation exclusive of reserves in the southeast corner
of the currently approved mining plan and Section 36 where coal reserves
are owned by the State of Montana, will be depleted in less than one
year.
Lengthy deferred development would almost certainly necessitate a close down of current operations. Royalties to the Tribe would cease, persons currently employed at the mine would be jobless, and the economic effects summarized previously under non-approval of the leases would occur.
The two different types of commissions discussed above would have similar responsibilities and effects only if both Indians and non-Indians are represented on the land use development program and commission board.
